canonical_topic: Pollution profile of nuclear power vs. fossil fuels
definition: Nuclear power produces no CO2, sulfur dioxide, or nitrogen oxide emissions, but concentrated nuclear waste poses an immediate, deadly health hazard that differs in kind from diffuse fossil-fuel pollution.
core_idea: The author contrasts fossil-fuel pollution, which mainly causes gradual harm (climate change, ecosystem damage) without an immediate lethal threat, against nuclear waste, which is deadly when concentrated and thus presents a direct, acute danger rather than a diffuse one.
key_points: Nuclear power generates no CO2, sulfur dioxide, or nitrogen oxide pollution.
Fossil fuel pollution is characterized as causing climate change, wildlife harm, and environmental damage, but not an immediate lethal threat to people.
Concentrated nuclear waste is deadly and presents an immediate health threat.
Storing concentrated nuclear waste safely is described as very problematic given its danger.
relationships: Builds on the earlier point that regulation forces nuclear waste to be concentrated rather than diluted.
caveats: "Nuclear is pollution-free" overlooks that the author distinguishes emissions-free operation from the separate, acute hazard posed by concentrated radioactive waste.
